exposure: Congenital heart disease (repaired tetralogy of Fallot/ventricular septal defect with pulmonary atresia)
Severe right ventricle to pulmonary artery conduit stenosis
cohort: The study describes a 29-year-old pregnant female with repaired tetralogy of Fallot or ventricular septal defect with pulmonary atresia, who presented with severe pulmonary conduit stenosis.
finding: Management of pregnant patients with adult congenital heart disease requires risk stratification, multidisciplinary team involvement, and individualized decisions regarding follow-up, anesthesia, and mode of delivery, with intervention for asymptomatic moderate to severe pulmonic stenosis potentially deferred until after delivery.
mod_finding: The decision for vaginal or cesarean delivery should be made on a case-by-case basis considering patient preference.
